title: Hot Baths May Help Your Heart, Study Finds
paragraphs: Many people enjoy a long, hot bath at the end of the day. But according to research, hot baths may do more than help you relax. They may also be good for your heart.

In Japan, taking a hot bath is a common daily habit. A study published in the journal Heart in 2020 looked at the bathing habits of more than 30,000 Japanese adults over a period of 20 years. The study was led by Dr. Hiroyasu Iso of Osaka University.

The researchers found that people who took a hot bath every day had a 28% lower risk of heart disease and a 26% lower risk of stroke than people who took baths only once or twice a week or not at all. People who took baths often were also less likely to develop high blood pressure, which may partly explain the result.

More recent research has also looked at hot baths. In a 2025 study from the University of Oregon in the US, 20 healthy young adults tried three types of heat: a hot bath, a traditional sauna and an infrared sauna. The researchers found that sitting in hot water caused the strongest effects on the heart and blood vessels.

Studies published in 2026 have given mixed results. A study in the journal Experimental Physiology found that one hot bath helped blood pressure fall more at night, which is a sign of healthy blood vessels. However, a review of many studies in the journal Physiology Reports found that the benefits of hot baths for heart health are still not clear.

However, the studies only show a link. They do not prove that hot baths protect the heart. Hot baths can also be dangerous for some people. In Japan, sudden deaths during hot baths are relatively common, especially in winter. Experts say that people with heart problems should talk to a doctor before taking very hot baths.
Also, baths should not replace exercise, which is still one of the best ways to keep your heart healthy.
